question: In 2018, India was the ______ producer of groundnut in the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is second largest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India is the world’s second largest producer of groundnut (मूंगफली), after China, which ranks first.

 

• As per 2018 data, China contributed roughly one-third of global groundnut production, with India following as the second largest producer.

 

• In India, Gujarat is the leading groundnut-producing state, followed by Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu.

 

• Groundnut (*Arachis hypogaea*) is a major kharif oilseed crop, grown mainly in semi-arid tropical and sub-tropical regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is among the world’s leading producers of oilseeds overall, along with soybean and mustard/rapeseed.

 

• Groundnut serves both as a source of edible oil and as a food crop (peanuts).

 

NOTE

 

• fourth largest (Option 1): Incorrect; India’s actual rank as a groundnut producer is second, not fourth.

 

• third largest (Option 2): Incorrect; the correct rank is second, not third.

 

• largest (Option 3): Incorrect; China, not India, is the world’s largest groundnut producer.

question: In 1929, under the presidency of ______, the Lahore Congress formalised the demand of Purna Swaraj.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (December 1929) was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru — his first term as Congress President. (लाहौर अधिवेशन — जवाहरलाल नेहरू)

 

• In this session, the Congress formally adopted the resolution of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as its goal, replacing the earlier demand for Dominion Status.

 

• The tricolour flag was hoisted on the banks of the river Ravi at midnight on 31 December 1929.

 

• 26 January was subsequently observed as “Purna Swaraj Day”/Independence pledge day from 1930 until 1947, and later chosen as the date the Constitution came into force in 1950 (Republic Day).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nehru went on to become independent India’s first Prime Minister.

 

• The Karachi Session (1931), presided over by Sardar Patel, adopted resolutions on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme.

 

NOTE

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 1): Presided over the 1931 Karachi Session, not the 1929 Lahore Session.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 2): Did not preside over the Lahore Session; he led the Dandi March (Civil Disobedience Movement) in 1930 that followed the Purna Swaraj resolution.

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose (Option 3): Presided over the Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939) Congress sessions, not Lahore 1929.

question:
Which of the following pairs regarding soil is correct?
I. Forest soil – These soils are loamy and silty in valley sides
II. Black soil – generally poor in phosphoric contents
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I: Forest soils, found in hilly and mountainous regions receiving adequate rainfall, are loamy and silty on valley sides while being coarse-grained on the upper slopes — this is correct.

 

• Statement II: Black soil (regur soil), formed from Deccan trap lava, is rich in lime, iron, magnesia and alumina but is generally poor in phosphoric content, nitrogen and organic matter — this is also correct.

 

• Since both statements accurately describe the respective soil types, the correct choice is “Both I and II”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Black soil is ideal for cotton cultivation and is also called “black cotton soil”.

 

• Forest soils vary structurally depending on the mountain environment where they occur — found on the slopes of the Himalayas, Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incorrect, since statement II about black soil is also correct.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, since statement I about forest soil is also correct.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both statements are factually accurate.

question:
Which of the following pair of "player – sports" is correct?
I. Anshu Malik – Boxing
II. Eldhose Paul – Triple Jump
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is incorrect: Anshu Malik is an Indian wrestler, not a boxer. She won a silver medal at the 2021 World Wrestling Championships (57 kg), becoming the first Indian woman wrestler to win a World Championship medal. (कुश्ती खिलाड़ी)

 

• Statement II is correct: Eldhose Paul is an Indian triple jumper who won the gold medal in men’s triple jump at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.

 

• Since only statement II is factually accurate, the correct choice is “Only II”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• At the same 2022 Commonwealth Games, Abdulla Aboobacker also won a medal (silver) in men’s triple jump, giving India a 1–2 finish alongside Eldhose Paul.

 

• Notable Indian boxers of this period include Nikhat Zareen, Lovlina Borgohain and Amit Panghal.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, since statement II is factually correct.

 

• Only I (Option 3): Incorrect, since statement I wrongly pairs Anshu Malik with boxing; she is actually a wrestler.

 

• Both I and II (Option 4): Incorrect, since statement I is false.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the stratosphere?
option_2: It extends up to a height of 50 km.
option_3: It contains a layer of ozone gas.
option_4: This layer is almost free from clouds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It lies above the mesosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The atmospheric layers, from the Earth’s surface upward, are: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere → Exosphere. So the stratosphere lies below the mesosphere, not above it — making this statement incorrect.

 

• The stratosphere extends from about 12 km to roughly 50 km above the Earth’s surface, which is accurately stated in option 2.

 

• It contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun (option 3 is correct).

 

• Since it has almost no water vapour or dust, the stratosphere is almost entirely free of clouds and is preferred for jet aircraft flight (option 4 is correct).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Temperature in the stratosphere increases with height (because ozone absorbs UV rays), unlike the troposphere where temperature decreases with height.

 

• The boundary between the troposphere and stratosphere is the tropopause; that between the stratosphere and mesosphere is the stratopause.

 

NOTE

 

• It extends up to a height of 50 km (Option 2): This is a correct statement about the stratosphere, so it is not the answer.

 

• It contains a layer of ozone gas (Option 3): This is also a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

 

• This layer is almost free from clouds (Option 4): This too is a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to start a new line in the same cell in MS-Excel 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alt + Enter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS-Excel 365, pressing Alt + Enter while typing inside a cell inserts a line break, letting you start a new line within the same cell.

 

• This differs from simply pressing Enter, which moves the cursor to the next cell/row instead of creating a new line in the same cell.

 

• This shortcut is widely used to neatly format multi-line text (such as addresses or notes) within a single cell.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Enabling “Wrap Text” (Home tab → Wrap Text) is often used together with Alt + Enter for readable multi-line cell content.

 

• Tab alone simply moves the active cell to the right; it does not create a line break.

 

NOTE

 

• Tab + Enter (Option 1): Not a valid shortcut for a line break within a cell.

 

• Ctrl + Enter (Option 3): This fills the same data into all selected cells at once, rather than creating a line break.

 

• Shift + Enter (Option 4): This typically moves the active cell one row up after entry, not a line break within the same cell.

question: Which of the following is correct regarding the Private Income?
option_1: Private Income = Factor income from net domestic product accruing to the private sector + National debt interest – Net factor income from abroad + Current transfers from government + Other net transfers from the rest of the world
option_2: Private Income = Factor income from net domestic product accruing to the private sector + National debt interest + Net factor income from abroad – Current transfers from government + Other net transfers from the rest of the world
option_3: Private Income = Factor income from net domestic product accruing to the private sector + National debt interest + Net factor income from abroad + Current transfers from government + Other net transfers from the rest of the world
option_4: Private Income = Factor income from net domestic product accruing to the private sector – National debt interest + Net factor income from abroad + Current transfers from government + Other net transfers from the rest of the world
solution_text:
The correct answer is Private Income = Factor income from net domestic product accruing to the private sector + National debt interest + Net factor income from abroad + Current transfers from government + Other net transfers from the rest of the world.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Private Income is a national-income aggregate measuring the total income received by private-sector enterprises and households from all sources, both domestic and foreign, through factor and transfer payments.

 

• As per the standard formula used in Indian macroeconomics, all five components are added together: factor income from net domestic product accruing to the private sector, national debt interest, net factor income from abroad, current transfers from the government, and other net transfers from the rest of the world.

 

• Getting the sign of even a single component wrong (as in the other three options) produces an incorrect formula.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Personal Income is derived from Private Income by subtracting corporate tax and the undistributed/retained profits of private corporations.

 

• Personal Disposable Income = Personal Income − Direct personal taxes − Miscellaneous fees/fines paid to the government.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrectly subtracts “Net factor income from abroad” instead of adding it.

 

• Option 2: Incorrectly subtracts “Current transfers from government” instead of adding it.

 

• Option 4: Incorrectly subtracts “National debt interest” instead of adding it.

question: Which of the following is the correct representation of number of atoms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is (given mass/molar mass) × Avogadro number.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The number of moles of a substance is calculated as: Number of moles = Given mass / Molar mass.

 

• The number of atoms (or molecules) in a given sample is obtained by multiplying the number of moles by Avogadro’s number (Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ per mole).

 

• Hence, the correct representation is: Number of atoms = (Given mass / Molar mass) × Avogadro number.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Avogadro’s number is named after the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro and represents the number of constituent particles present in one mole of a substance.

 

• Molar mass is numerically equal to the atomic/molecular mass of a substance expressed in grams per mole (g/mol).

 

NOTE

 

• (avogadro number/given mass) × molar mass (Option 2): This arrangement is formulaically incorrect for computing the number of atoms.

 

• (molar mass/given mass) × Avogadro number (Option 3): This inverts the mass/molar-mass ratio, giving an incorrect formula.

 

• (given mass/ Avogadro number) × molar mass (Option 4): This wrongly divides by Avogadro’s number instead of multiplying by it.

question:
Identify the person from the given statements.
Popularly known as the “King of Pop”, the best-selling American singer, songwriter and dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Michael Jackson.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Michael Jackson, popularly known as the “King of Pop”, was a best-selling American singer, songwriter and dancer. (माइकल जैक्सन — “पॉप के बादशाह”)

 

• He is regarded as one of the most significant cultural figures of the 20th century, known for albums like “Thriller” (the best-selling album of all time) and his innovative dance moves such as the moonwalk.

 

• He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and won numerous Grammy Awards during his career.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Michael Jackson began his career as a child performer with the Jackson 5 before pursuing a highly successful solo career.

 

• He passed away in June 2009, but his cultural and musical influence remains widely celebrated.

 

NOTE

 

• Benny Andersson (Option 1): A Swedish musician and member of the pop group ABBA, not known as the “King of Pop”.

 

• John Lennon (Option 2): An English musician, singer-songwriter and co-founder of The Beatles, not associated with the title “King of Pop”.

 

• Elton John (Option 3): A British singer-songwriter and pianist known for hits like “Rocket Man”, not the “King of Pop”.

question: Which of the following comes under 5th schedule of the Indian constitution?
option_1: Provisions related to Schedule Areas and Scheduled Tribes
option_2: Provisions related to Tribal areas in states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
option_3: Provisions related to Oaths or Affirmations
solution_text:
The correct answer is Provisions related to Schedule Areas and Scheduled Tribes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram (which are covered under the Sixth Schedule instead). (पांचवीं अनुसूची — अनुसूचित क्षेत्र एवं अनुसूचित जनजाति)

 

• It provides for a Tribes Advisory Council in states having Scheduled Areas, and empowers the Governor to modify the application of central/state laws to such areas.

 

• This Schedule falls under Article 244(1) of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sixth Schedule (Article 244(2)) deals with the administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram through Autonomous District Councils.

 

• The Third Schedule contains the forms of oaths or affirmations, while the Eighth Schedule lists the officially recognised languages of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Provisions related to Tribal areas in states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram (Option 2): This is covered under the Sixth Schedule, not the Fifth.

 

• Provisions related to Oaths or Affirmations (Option 3): This is covered under the Third Schedule.

 

• Provisions related to Languages (Option 4): This is covered under the Eighth Schedule.

NOTE

 

• Microsoft (Option 1): Elon Musk is not associated with Microsoft.

 

• Adobe Inc (Option 3): Elon Musk has no leadership role at Adobe.

 

• Flipkart (Option 4): An Indian e-commerce company; Elon Musk has no connection to it.

question: World Environment Day is held every year on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5th June.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• World Environment Day is observed every year on 5th June to raise global awareness about environmental protection and encourage political attention and public action.

 

• It was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1972, following the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment.

 

• Each year, a different country hosts the official global celebrations, with a specific environmental theme highlighted.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• World Environment Day is coordinated by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).

 

• Related observances include World Ozone Day (16 September) and World Earth Day (22 April).

 

NOTE

 

• 1st January (Option 2): Marks New Year’s Day, not World Environment Day.

 

• 29th August (Option 3): Not associated with World Environment Day.

 

• 1st July (Option 4): Observed as Doctor’s Day in India, not World Environment Day.

question: Which among the following is the largest container port in India as of October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru Port.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of October 2022, Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), located near Mumbai, Maharashtra, was the largest container port in India in terms of container traffic handled.

 

• It is India’s premier container-handling port and among the top container ports globally by capacity.

 

• The port has multiple container terminals and plays a critical role in India’s foreign trade, particularly containerised cargo.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• JNPT was commissioned in 1989 and is one of the 12 major ports of India, administered by the central government.

 

• Other significant container-handling ports in India include Chennai Port, Mundra Port (private) and Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar) Port.

 

NOTE

 

• Port Blair (Option 1): A port in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, not among India’s major container ports.

 

• Tuticorin Port (Option 2): Also known as V.O. Chidambaranar Port in Tamil Nadu, but with far lower container traffic than JNPT.

 

• Paradip Port (Option 3): Located in Odisha, primarily known for handling bulk cargo like coal and iron ore, not the largest for containers.

question: The part VII of the Indian constitution has been omitted. It is related with which of the following?
option_2: States in part B of the first schedule
option_3: Armed forces in states in part A of the second schedule
option_4: Reservation for Anglo –Indian communities in parliament
solution_text:
The correct answer is States in part B of the first schedule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part VII of the Indian Constitution originally dealt with the States in Part B of the First Schedule (former princely states/unions classified as “Part B States” under the original constitutional scheme).

 

• This Part was omitted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956, which reorganised Indian states on a linguistic basis and abolished the four-fold classification of states into Part A, B, C and D.

 

• Since the classification of states into Parts A, B, C and D ceased to exist after the 1956 reorganisation, Part VII became redundant and was removed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The States Reorganisation Act, 1956, along with the Seventh Amendment, replaced the earlier four-category classification with a single category of “States” and “Union Territories”.

 

• Article 238, dealing with the constitutional application to Part B states, was also omitted by the same amendment.

 

NOTE

 

• Provision relating to property (Option 1): Originally covered under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31, significantly altered/omitted by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, not Part VII.

 

• Armed forces in states in part A of the second schedule (Option 3): Not the subject of the omitted Part VII; the Second Schedule deals with salaries/allowances of constitutional functionaries.

 

• Reservation for Anglo–Indian communities in parliament (Option 4): Covered under Article 331 (since lapsed), not Part VII.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the features of a perfectly competitive market?
I. The market consists of a large number of buyers and sellers.
II. Information is perfect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: A perfectly competitive market is characterised by the presence of a very large number of buyers and sellers, none of whom can individually influence the market price.

 

• Statement II is correct: Perfect information is another essential feature — all buyers and sellers have complete knowledge of prices and product quality, so no seller can charge more than the prevailing market price.

 

• Since both statements accurately describe essential features of a perfectly competitive market, the correct choice is “Both I and II”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other features of a perfectly competitive market include homogeneous products, free entry and exit of firms, and perfect mobility of factors of production.

 

• Under perfect competition, firms are “price takers”, as market price is determined by overall demand and supply, not by individual firms.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since statement II regarding perfect information is also a valid feature.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, since both statements correctly describe features of a perfectly competitive market.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, since statement I regarding a large number of buyers and sellers is also valid.

question: Which among the following dance forms is not related to Karnataka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rauf.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rauf (also spelt Roufh) is a traditional folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir, performed mainly by women during festivals and the harvest/spring season — it is not related to Karnataka.

 

• Huttari, Suggi (Suggi Kunitha) and Karaga are all traditional folk dances originating from Karnataka.

 

• Huttari is a harvest dance of the Kodava (Coorg) community, Suggi is a spring/harvest folk dance, and Karaga is a ritualistic folk dance associated with the worship of Draupadi Amma, performed in Bengaluru.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable folk dances of Karnataka include Yakshagana (a dance-drama form), Dollu Kunitha (drum dance), and Veeragase.

 

• Other folk dance forms of Kashmir include Dumhal, performed by the Wattal tribe.

 

NOTE

 

• Huttari (Option 2): A harvest-festival dance of the Kodava community of Karnataka, so it is related to Karnataka.

 

• Suggi (Option 3): A folk dance of Karnataka performed to celebrate the spring/harvest season, so it is related to Karnataka.

 

• Karaga (Option 4): A traditional festival dance of Karnataka associated with the Karaga festival in Bengaluru, so it is related to Karnataka.

question: Akham Lakshmi Devi received the sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for her contribution to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri Dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Akham Lakshmi Devi, a veteran exponent of Manipuri dance, was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for her contribution to Manipuri Dance. (मणिपुरी नृत्य)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is India’s highest national recognition given to practising artists in the fields of music, dance and drama.

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, closely associated with Vaishnavite themes and the Raas Leela tradition of Manipur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952 and is the first National Academy of the Arts set up by the Government of India.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Bharatnatyam Dance (Option 1): A classical dance form originating in Tamil Nadu, not the field for which Akham Lakshmi Devi was honoured.

 

• Kathak Dance (Option 3): A classical dance form of North India, unrelated to her contribution.

 

• Sattriya Dance (Option 4): A classical dance form of Assam, distinct from Manipuri dance.

question: Which of the following Harappan town was located on Khadir Beyt in the Runn of Kutch and was divided into three parts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dholavira.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dholavira is a major Harappan (Indus Valley Civilization) site located on Khadir Bet (island) in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat. (ढोलावीरा — हड़प्पा सभ्यता का स्थल)

 

• The site is unique for being divided into three fortified parts: the citadel (acropolis), the middle town, and the lower town — a distinctive urban-planning feature not commonly seen at other Harappan sites.

 

• Dholavira is also notable for its sophisticated water conservation system, including large stepped reservoirs, and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dholavira was excavated by archaeologist R.S. Bisht of the Archaeological Survey of India.

 

• Other important Harappan sites in Gujarat include Lothal (known for its dockyard) and Surkotada.

 

NOTE

 

• Sotka-koh (Option 1): A Harappan site located in present-day Balochistan, Pakistan, not in the Rann of Kutch.

 

• Chanhudaro (Option 2): A Harappan site in Sindh, Pakistan, known for bead-making and craft production, not on Khadir Bet.

 

• Surkotada (Option 3): A Harappan site in Gujarat’s Rann of Kutch region, notable for horse remains, but not divided into three parts like Dholavira.

question: Which team was the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) Season 8 winner?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dabang Delhi K.C..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dabang Delhi K.C. won the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) Season 8, held in December 2021, by defeating Patna Pirates in the final.

 

• This was Dabang Delhi K.C.’s first PKL title.

 

• PKL Season 8 was played entirely in Bengaluru, Karnataka, due to COVID-19 protocols.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Patna Pirates, the runners-up in Season 8, are historically one of the most successful PKL franchises, having won three consecutive titles in Seasons 3, 4 and 5.

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League was launched in 2014 and has significantly popularised the sport of kabaddi in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Bengal Warriors (Option 1): Won the PKL Season 7 title (2019), not Season 8.

 

• Bengaluru Bulls (Option 2): Won the PKL Season 6 title (2018), not Season 8.

 

• Patna Pirates (Option 4): Were the runners-up in Season 8, having lost the final to Dabang Delhi K.C.

question: Behind the cornea, there is a dark muscular structure called the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is iris.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The iris is the dark, coloured, muscular structure located behind the cornea in the human eye. (आइरिस — परितारिका)

 

• It controls the amount of light entering the eye by adjusting the size of the pupil (the central opening within the iris) through contraction and relaxation of its muscles.

 

• The pigmentation of the iris determines a person’s eye colour (e.g., brown, blue, green).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The retina is the innermost, light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that converts light into neural signals sent to the brain via the optic nerve.

 

• The lens, located just behind the iris and pupil, focuses light onto the retina by changing its shape (accommodation).

 

NOTE

 

• retina (Option 1): The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, not the structure directly behind the cornea.

 

• pupil (Option 2): The opening at the centre of the iris through which light enters; it is an aperture, not itself a muscular structure.

 

• lens (Option 4): A transparent, flexible structure that focuses light onto the retina, located behind the iris, not the dark muscular structure described.

question: Which of the statements is NOT correct regarding energy?
option_1: The energy possessed by a body due to its change in position or shape is called the potential energy.
option_2: An object of mass m moving with velocity v has a kinetic energy of (mv) /2.
option_3: The gravitational potential energy of an object of mass, M raised through a height, H from the earth’s surface is given by MgH.
option_4: An object in motion possesses what is known as the kinetic energy of the object.
solution_text:
The correct answer is An object of mass m moving with velocity v has a kinetic energy of (mv) /2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct formula for the kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving with velocity v is KE = (1/2)mv² — half the product of mass and the square of velocity.

 

• The statement in option 2 gives the kinetic energy as “(mv)/2”, i.e., half the product of mass and velocity (without squaring velocity) — this is not the correct kinetic-energy formula, making this the incorrect statement.

 

• Statement 1 is correct: potential energy is indeed the energy possessed by a body due to its change in position or shape (e.g., gravitational PE, elastic PE).

 

• Statement 3 is correct: gravitational potential energy is given by PE = MgH, where M is mass, g is acceleration due to gravity, and H is height above the earth’s surface.

 

• Statement 4 is correct: an object in motion possesses kinetic energy — motion is the defining condition for kinetic energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of both kinetic and potential energy is the joule (J).

 

• The work-energy theorem states that the work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.

 

NOTE

 

• The energy possessed by a body due to its change in position or shape is called the potential energy. (Option 1): This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

 

• The gravitational potential energy of an object of mass, M raised through a height, H from the earth’s surface is given by MgH. (Option 3): This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

 

• An object in motion possesses what is known as the kinetic energy of the object. (Option 4): This is a correct statement, so it is not the answer.

question: Which of the following is a magnetic disk?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Winchester.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Winchester disk (an early term for what is now commonly called a hard disk drive) is a type of magnetic storage disk that uses magnetic material to store data.

 

• Magnetic disks store data using magnetised regions on a spinning platter and can be read from and written to repeatedly using a magnetic read/write head.

 

• DVD, CD-RW and CD-R are all optical storage media, which use laser light to read and write data, not magnetism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term “Winchester disk” originated from an early IBM hard disk drive (IBM 3340), whose 30MB fixed / 30MB removable storage configuration was reminiscent of the “.30-30” Winchester rifle cartridge, giving rise to the nickname.

 

• Magnetic tape is another common magnetic storage medium, often used for data backup.

 

NOTE

 

• DVD (Option 2): An optical disk that uses laser technology to read/write data, not a magnetic disk.

 

• CD-RW (Option 3): A rewritable optical disk that uses laser technology, not magnetic storage.

 

• CD-R (Option 4): A recordable (write-once) optical disk that uses laser technology, not magnetic storage.
